request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The rollover now also soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open, in
start-date order, each as a soft close would (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED), after the ROLLOVER line.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollover now soft-closes every period of the old fiscal year that is still open. It does them in start-date order and writes one `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED` line each, after the `ROLLOVER` line. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What changed** (server only; the front end and stored data needed nothing new):
- **`PeriodService.java`**: I moved the existing soft-close step (fix the figures, save, write the audit line) into a private `softCloseNow`. The normal soft close and a new `softCloseOpen(sheetId, user, periods)` both use it. `softCloseOpen` skips periods that are already closed or soft-closed. For example, in the test 2026-11 was closed beforehand and gets no line.
- **`RolloverService.java`**: right after writing `ROLLOVER`, it calls `softCloseOpen` on the old year's periods. I updated the class comment to match.

**Two things to know:**
- **No separate role check:** the rollover already requires a steward, so these automatic soft closes don't re-check the "close" permission the way the soft-close button does.
- **Undo doesn't reopen them:** undoing a rollover still removes its new periods and takes back its opening balances, but the old year's periods stay soft-closed. The request didn't cover undo and the test doesn't exercise it. If undo should reopen them, the rollover record would also need to store which periods it soft-closed.
